Best,

Hi Jaspreet / team — thanks for the note. Attaching a draft On-Prem/Offline SIG addendum and a blank transfer manifest template to make review easier. High level summary below:

- Offline artifact delivery: For air-gapped customers we provide an encrypted, signed update package containing binaries, schema, and install manifests. Packages are PGP-signed by Redwood release engineering; manifests include SHA256 checksums and human-readable install steps. Delivery options: encrypted physical media (FIPS-certified drive) or sealed AWS Snowball / air-gapped transfer via customer-provided removable media. All shipments include a tamper-evident seal and a transfer manifest.

- Verification: Each package includes a signed manifest and verification script. Operators must verify the manifest signature and checksums before applying updates; steps are included in the manifest. We can provide a short runbook for your ops team and remote verification support during the first transfer window.

- Evidence artifacts: For your SIG we can provide redacted SOC 2 artifacts, architecture diagrams, change logs for the package, and a chain-of-custody form signed by our shipping partner. Where full logs are restricted, we provide attestations and extracted-event summaries.

- Update cadence & emergency patches: Standard cadence is quarterly offline update bundles plus ad-hoc emergency hotfixes for critical CVEs. For hotfixes, we offer an accelerated packaging and delivery path (24–72 hour packaging window), plus an option for on-site certified engineer assistance via our partner network if required.

- Support model & SLAs: For air-gapped deployments we offer a tiered support model:
  * Standard: email + ticketing, 72-hour response for severity 1 (business-impacting) incidents related to offline packages.
  * Enterprise: 24/7 phone escalation + designated account engineer, 12-hour response, 72-hour on-site option (where contract includes travel).

- Chain-of-custody / custody transfer: We record shipment manifests and electronic signatures at handoff. Physical shipments include tamper proof seals and handoff signatures. Digital transfers use signed manifests and hardware HSM-based encryption where requested.

Next steps I suggest: 1) Review the attached addendum and manifest template, 2) Mark up comments inline (I flagged a couple of optional clauses), 3) If acceptable, we will route the final addendum to DocuSign and schedule your preferred transfer window.

I've cc'd Priyom (solutions) to confirm packaging and verification steps and Rishi (legal) for the addendum language.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole

Marissa / Jaspreet — quick technical clarifications from our side: 

1) Packaging format: we will provide a tarball (.tar.gz) with a top-level manifest.json and a PGP-signed detached signature (.sig). The manifest is intentionally small and human-readable (we can also provide a YAML variant).
2) KV cache / model weights: for air-gapped customers we deliver model artifacts (quantized weights) and runtime binaries. There is no external fetching at boot — the serving runtime includes an integrity check that rejects packages whose manifest/signature verification fails.
3) Operator verification steps: we recommend three-tier verification: signature -> checksum -> dry-run (local verification script). I'll attach a sample operator verification checklist to the final SOW.

If ACME requires HSM-wrapped keys or an escrow deposit of keys, we support integration with customer KMS and an optional key-escrow workflow (offline transfer of wrapped keys with separate channel).

Let me know if you want this expanded into a short one-page ops checklist for your runbook.

-Priyom
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa / Priyom — this is helpful. A few items security wants clarified before we proceed: 

- SLA for emergency patch delivery: we need an explicit RTO commitment for critical CVEs that have an exploit in the wild. Can Redwood commit to an X-hour packaging window and a Y-hour delivery/start window for Enterprise customers?
- Chain-of-custody evidence: we need the template you mentioned (signed by carrier + Redwood). Can you confirm the carrier partners you use and whether you can provide scanned handoff signatures?
- Physical delivery windows: our ops team needs a preferred delivery window (e.g., Mon–Thu 09:00–16:00 local) to accept sealed media. Can Redwood accommodate scheduling and provide a single POC who signs the transfer manifest?

If you can add those clarifications into the addendum (or attachments) we'll review with procurement today. We may request an explicit on-site assistance SLA as an add-on.

Jaspreet

Jaspreet — great questions, and we can fold these into the addendum. Proposed concrete language (summary):

- Emergency patch RTO (Enterprise): packaging within 24 hours of triage + delivery initiation within 48 hours for supported regions (US/EU). Standard customers: packaging within 72 hours. We will include optional on-site dispatch SLA as an add-on (72-hour guaranteed on-site target, travel-dependent).
- Chain-of-custody: carrier partners include SecureShip Partners and IronLogistics; we will provide scanned handoff signatures and a signed chain-of-custody PDF for each shipment. The transfer manifest template (attached earlier) will include courier name, AWB tracking, timestamp, and signatory name.
- Delivery windows / POC: we can accommodate Mon–Thu 09:00–16:00 local delivery windows. Redwood will nominate a single transfer coordinator for the shipment; the coordinator's name and contact will be listed in the final manifest.

Next steps: 1) I'll incorporate the RTO and chain-of-custody language into SIG_OnPrem_Addendum_v2 and circulate for redlines, 2) If ACME is ready, I will send the DocuSign packet for the addendum and SOW (link below), 3) After signature we schedule a 2-week transfer window and Redwood will run the verification session with your operators.
